original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. lean-mend has the operation setOptionBefore name value. It puts set_option name value in before a declaration, and no heartbeats operation remains. A rule whose operations are all setOptionBefore runs after every other rule of its entrenchment. Three rules use it: backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false (v4.33.0 #13895), maxRecDepth (v4.33.0 #13956), and backward.do.legacy true (v4.32.0 #13305). Decisions B1, B2 and B3 of docs/breaking-changes.md hold.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. LeanMend/Spec/Types.lean EditOp has heartbeats (n : Nat), which inserts only set_option maxHeartbeats n in. No operation inserts any other option. rules/proposed has no rule for #13895, #13956 or #13305.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run lake test: tests/OpsTest.lean shows setOptionBefore producing the inserted text before a declaration, and a setOptionBefore rule ordered after another rule of the same entrenchment. A fixture under tests/ whose declaration fails under the v4.33.1 transparency default and builds with the option shows the rule accepted, through a runner that sources tests/lib/report.sh. Run scripts/gate.sh: stdout is one JSON object; the key 'steps.set_option before a declaration.ok' is true, and failed is 0.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Spec and Core import no Shell module (scripts/gate.sh checks it). Termination stays a theorem in LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean, with no retry cap and no timeout as a control. Decision D10 holds: lean-mend adds no declaration to a target. lean-mend depends on Lean core only, not on Mathlib. Every committed text is in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Run export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH" before a lean or lake command. Scratch files go in the gitignored .scratch/ directory, not /tmp. The worker task timeout is 3600 seconds. Do not run lean-mend on EVMLean: one EVMLean run takes about 2 hours, and the operator runs it after the merge.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) LeanMend/Spec/Types.lean, LeanMend/Core/Ops.lean, LeanMend/Shell/Parse.lean, rules/proposed/, docs/rules.md, tests/
restatement: lean-mend replaces its heartbeats operation with one general operation, setOptionBefore name value, which puts 'set_option name value in' before a declaration. A rule whose operations are all setOptionBefore runs after every other rule of its entrenchment, because an option hides a change instead of adapting the source. Three proposed rules use it: backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false (v4.33.0 #13895), maxRecDepth (v4.33.0 #13956) and backward.do.legacy true (v4.32.0 #13305). The existing constraints keep holding: Spec and Core import no Shell module, termination stays a theorem, lean-mend adds no declaration to a target, and it needs Lean core only.

restatement_clauses.text: EditOp in LeanMend/Spec/Types.lean has the operation setOptionBefore name value and no heartbeats operation remains.
setOptionBefore puts 'set_option name value in' before a declaration, shown by tests/OpsTest.lean under lake test, and the scripts/gate.sh step 'set_option before a declaration' has ok true.
A rule whose operations are all setOptionBefore runs after every other rule of its entrenchment, shown by a tests/OpsTest.lean case.

rules/proposed holds rules for backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false (v4.33.0 #13895), maxRecDepth (v4.33.0 #13956) and backward.do.legacy true (v4.32.0 #13305), each using setOptionBefore.
A fixture under tests/ whose declaration fails under the v4.33.1 transparency default and builds with the option shows the rule accepted, through a runner that sources tests/lib/report.sh.
scripts/gate.sh prints one JSON object on stdout, and failed is 0.
Spec and Core import no Shell module, and lean-mend depends on Lean core only, not on Mathlib.
Termination stays a theorem in LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean, and docs/rules.md describes setOptionBefore.

goal: lean-mend gets one operation, setOptionBefore, that puts a set_option line before a declaration. It replaces heartbeats. Rules that only use it run last. Three rules use it.

The operations test file has a case for a rule ordered after another rule of the same entrenchment.
The proposed rules folder names all three option rules.
A test runner script under tests sources the shared report library.
The project gate finishes with no failed step.
No Spec or Core file imports a Shell module.
The termination file still states a theorem.
